stories.headline: HART OS: Open‑Source AI OS That Runs Frontier Models Without a Data Center
stories.summary: The HART OS project provides an open‑source operating system that enables cutting‑edge AI models to run on consumer‑grade hardware, sidestepping the need for massive data centers. Built with performance in mind, it aims to democratize access to powerful AI capabilities.

stories.headline: Data‑Oriented Design Primer: Boosting Game Performance Through Memory Layout
stories.summary: The PDF introduces data‑oriented design principles, emphasizing how arranging data for cache friendliness can dramatically speed up game engines. It contrasts this approach with traditional object‑oriented methods and offers concrete implementation tips.

stories.headline: The New AI Superpowers: Why Focus and Follow‑Through Matter More Than Hype
stories.summary: The essay argues that lasting AI leadership will depend on disciplined execution and sustained investment rather than fleeting hype. It calls on policymakers and businesses to prioritize strategic focus to harness AI’s transformative potential.

stories.headline: Pitchfork Revisits Janet’s Overlooked 2001 Album, Uncovering Its Emotional Riches
stories.summary: Pitchfork’s deep‑dive reexamines Janet’s 2001 record, highlighting its lush emotional texture and its place at a pivotal career moment. The piece argues the album deserves greater recognition for its artistic ambition.

stories.headline: US Halts Iran Strikes for Second Day, Tehran Mirrors Pause Amid Ceasefire Talks
stories.summary: For the second consecutive day, the United States paused its missile attacks on Iran, and Tehran announced a reciprocal halt. Both sides say the de‑escalation is a step toward negotiating a temporary ceasefire.

stories.headline: Terence Tao Explores How AI Is Reshaping Modern Mathematics
stories.summary: In his lecture slides, mathematician Terence Tao outlines how AI tools are changing the way conjectures are generated and proofs are verified. He discusses both the opportunities for accelerating discovery and the new challenges for the discipline.

stories.headline: Four Practical Steps to Prevent Burnout in Children’s Ministry Volunteers
stories.summary: The article presents four actionable strategies—clear boundaries, supportive community, ongoing training, and intentional rest—to curb volunteer fatigue in children’s ministries. Implementing these measures aims to sustain healthy, effective ministry teams.

stories.headline: Israeli Settlers Accused of Arson on Mosques, Cars and Farms in West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinian sources report that Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, vehicles, and agricultural land in the West Bank, intensifying regional tensions. The attacks follow a recent clash that left casualties on both sides.

stories.headline: 12‑Year‑Old Builds Robots That Speak Endangered Indigenous Languages
stories.summary: Guided by a mentor, a 12‑year‑old in Michigan programmed robots to converse in threatened Native American languages. The project showcases how technology can aid in preserving linguistic heritage.

stories.headline: CheapSecurity Offers Lightweight, Self‑Hosted CCTV for Linux SBCs
stories.summary: CheapSecurity is an open‑source CCTV solution optimized for low‑cost single‑board computers like the Raspberry Pi. It provides a privacy‑focused, self‑hosted alternative to cloud‑based video surveillance systems.

stories.headline: Gatwick Rolls Out Autonomous Parking System
stories.summary: London Gatwick Airport has partnered with Stanley Robotics to introduce a self‑driving car‑parking service that shuttles vehicles to and from the terminal. The pilot aims to cut wait times and free up space, marking the UK’s first large‑scale robotic parking deployment.

stories.headline: Google Reveals $94 B SpaceX Holding, Securing 6% Stake
stories.summary: In a recent filing, Alphabet disclosed it owns roughly $94.1 billion of SpaceX shares, giving it a six‑percent ownership of Elon Musk’s rocket company. The revelation underscores Google’s growing interest in the commercial space sector.

stories.headline: GrapheneOS Adds New Defenses Against Locked‑Device Data Extraction
stories.summary: The privacy‑focused Android fork has implemented hardware‑backed safeguards that block forensic tools from pulling data from a locked phone. These measures rely on verified boot and encrypted storage to keep user information sealed when the device is unattended.

stories.headline: Police Kill Berlin Pride Attacker After Knife Rush
stories.summary: Authorities said Abdul Ballout was fatally shot when he lunged at officers with a knife during the Pride march in Berlin’s western district. The incident follows a separate vehicle‑ramming that injured dozens earlier in the day.

stories.headline: Inside the Shadowy Relay Market Fueling LLM Token Resale and Fraud
stories.summary: Matt Lenhard’s investigation uncovers a network that aggregates API keys to sell discounted large‑language‑model tokens, primarily operating out of China. The scheme enables resellers to undercut official pricing while exposing users to potential abuse and security risks.

stories.headline: Berlin Pride Ramming Attack Draws Condemnation from Chancellor
stories.summary: A driver plowed a vehicle into a crowd of Pride participants, prompting German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to label the act “heinous.” The assault left many injured and sparked a nationwide debate on public safety at large events.

stories.headline: Decker Revives HyperCard‑Style App Building for Modern macOS
stories.summary: Decker is a new development environment that lets users create interactive cards and scripts, echoing the classic HyperCard experience on today’s macOS. It targets creators who want rapid prototyping without deep coding expertise.

stories.headline: War‑Displaced Lebanese Turn to Satellite Imagery to Check Home Damage
stories.summary: Families forced from southern Lebanon are purchasing high‑resolution satellite photos to see whether their houses survived Israel’s recent incursion. The costly service offers a rare glimpse of property status when on‑the‑ground access is impossible.

stories.headline: Women’s ADHD Often Missed, Carrying Unique Health Risks
stories.summary: Research shows that ADHD symptoms in females frequently differ from the classic hyperactive presentation, leading to underdiagnosis into adulthood. Untreated ADHD in women is linked to higher rates of anxiety, depression, and other chronic conditions.

stories.headline: Rising Heat and Smoke Endanger Traditional Summer Activities for Kids
stories.summary: Extreme temperatures and wildfire smoke are forcing parents to rethink outdoor plans that once defined the school break. Experts warn that climate‑driven disruptions could reshape how families spend summer in the coming decades.

stories.headline: Turning a ThinkPad T480 into a Mobile Phone
stories.summary: A DIY guide shows how to repurpose a ThinkPad T480 as a handheld phone by combining its built‑in LTE modem with custom software. The project demonstrates the flexibility of modern laptops for unconventional uses.

stories.headline: Berlin Pride Attack Suspect Confirmed Dead, Police Say
stories.summary: German authorities have confirmed that the 21‑year‑old suspect in the Berlin Pride vehicle attack is dead. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt labeled the incident a likely Islamic terror attack, identifying the suspect as Abdul Ballout, a German‑born man of Lebanese descent.

stories.headline: Wildfires Displace Over 300,000 Across France and Spain
stories.summary: Massive fires forced the evacuation of roughly 50,000 residents in France and triggered a broader displacement of more than 300,000 people in the region. At least one fatality has been reported in Spain as authorities battle the blazes.

stories.headline: Inside the Token Relay Market Fueling Crypto Fraud
stories.summary: An investigative piece uncovers how a relay ecosystem enables token resellers to skim profits and facilitate scams. The article details the mechanics, participants, and regulatory challenges of this opaque market.

stories.headline: Footage from Berlin Pride Attack Scene as Manhunt Persists
stories.summary: Video from the crime scene shows police cordoning off the area after the vehicle attack during Berlin's Pride parade. While a 21‑year‑old suspect has been identified, he remains at large.

stories.headline: Show HN: Reverse Minesweeper – A New Puzzle Twist
stories.summary: A developer released Reverse Minesweeper, a web game where players place mines instead of avoiding them. The twist challenges traditional logic and offers a fresh take on the classic puzzle genre.

stories.headline: Go Analysis Framework Enables Modular Static Analysis
stories.summary: The Go team launched a new analysis framework that lets developers build and combine static analysis tools easily. Its modular design aims to streamline code inspection across Go projects.

stories.headline: Kill The Cookie Banner – EU Tool to Block Consent Pop‑ups
stories.summary: Kill The Cookie Banner is an open‑source initiative that automatically hides intrusive cookie consent notices across European websites. The project seeks to improve user experience while respecting privacy regulations.

stories.headline: Works & Wonders July 26 Edition Highlights Music and Devotion
stories.summary: The latest Works & Wonders newsletter features tracks like "Sounds of the Forest" and a devotional piece to start the Lord's Day. It also references previous editions from May and April.

stories.headline: Alex Eala’s Wimbledon Run Sparks Tennis Boom in the Philippines
stories.summary: Filipino teen Alex Eala’s impressive performance at Wimbledon has ignited widespread interest in tennis across the country. The sport, once seen as elite, is now gaining traction among everyday Filipinos.

stories.headline: Cutting Through the Noise: Simple Ways to Block Bad Bots
stories.summary: The guide walks through practical techniques—like CAPTCHAs, rate limiting, and user‑agent filtering—to keep unwanted bots at bay. It also highlights trade‑offs between security and user experience when implementing these measures.

stories.headline: Wildfire Near Bordeaux Forces Tens of Thousands to Flee
stories.summary: Firefighters are battling a fast‑moving blaze near Bordeaux, prompting the evacuation of tens of thousands of residents. The incident is part of a broader fire emergency that has displaced over 330,000 people across France and Spain.

stories.headline: French Firefighters Confront Rare Pyrocumulonimbus Storm
stories.summary: While suppressing wildfires in southwestern France, crews encountered a pyrocumulonimbus, a towering fire‑generated thunderstorm. The sudden lightning and gusty winds from the cloud complicated containment efforts and marked a first for French firefighters.

stories.headline: Design Is Always a Trade‑off, Not a Perfection
stories.summary: The essay argues that every design decision balances competing constraints, making compromise inevitable. Effective designers identify the optimal middle ground to deliver functional and aesthetically pleasing solutions.

stories.headline: htmx 4.0 Goes Retro, Launches Exclusively on Game Boy
stories.summary: htmx 4.0 has been released as a JavaScript library that runs solely on the original Game Boy, turning the handheld into a quirky web‑development platform. The stunt underscores the library’s minimal footprint and the community’s playful spirit.

stories.headline: Pogačar Wins Fifth Tour de France as Wildfire Response Trims Final Stage
stories.summary: Slovenian rider Tadej Pogačar secured his fifth Tour de France victory, edging out rivals in a shortened final stage. Police and security forces were redeployed to fight wildfires in southwest France, forcing organizers to cut the stage length.

stories.headline: Ruff 0.16.0 Rolls Out New Checks, Breaking Some CI Pipelines
stories.summary: Ruff version 0.16.0 introduced new default linting rules that caused several continuous‑integration jobs to fail. The update highlights the tool’s rapid development pace and the importance of pinning dependencies in CI pipelines.

stories.headline: Progressive Democrats Ride Winning Streak, Yet Swing Voters Remain Elusive
stories.summary: Left‑leaning Democrats have enjoyed a recent string of electoral wins, but their appeal to working‑class swing voters remains uncertain. The upcoming Michigan race will test whether their progressive platform can attract those crucial voters.

stories.headline: Italian Kids Overweight Despite Mediterranean Roots, WHO Warns
stories.summary: New WHO data shows Italian children are among the most overweight in Europe, despite the country’s famed Mediterranean diet. Increased consumption of pizza, pasta, and processed carbs is driving the rise in childhood obesity.

stories.headline: Practical Tips for Writing Clear, Compelling English Prose
stories.summary: The piece offers concrete advice for writing clear English prose, emphasizing active voice, concise sentences, and logical flow. It provides actionable steps that writers can apply immediately to improve readability and impact.

stories.headline: The Strongest El Niño Ever
Public Media Reinvents Itself After Federal Funding Ends
stories.summary: One year after the Trump administration eliminated decades‑long federal support, public radio and TV stations are scrambling to innovate and cut costs. While new revenue models spark creativity, many outlets remain uneasy about long‑term sustainability.

stories.headline: New Bell Prison Launches In‑House Record Label, Turns Inmates into Musicians
stories.summary: In Cameroon's notorious New Bell jail, a self‑run label lets prisoners record songs and videos from their cells. The program aims to rehabilitate inmates and generate income, though critics question its impact on justice.

stories.headline: Flatiron Icon Fetches $58.5 Million in Luxury Redevelopment Deal
stories.summary: After a multi‑year renovation, the historic Flatiron Building is poised for a high‑end residential conversion priced at $58.5 million. Buyers will pay a premium for its landmark status and ultra‑modern amenities.

stories.headline: Love Island Mirrors Britain’s Shift Toward More Progressive Dating Norms
stories.summary: The reality show now showcases women initiating romance and a broader spectrum of relationship styles. Analysts say the series reflects a cultural move away from traditional courtship toward more fluid, egalitarian connections.
